summary: Regression-tested the contact/email escaping fixes, admin auth, service-page SEO, card navigation/accessibility, and embedded service contact form against the public preview URL. All requested backend contact/auth behaviors passed, the frontend production build passed, canonical and og:url are corrected, all card/form flows passed, but the three JSON-LD scripts are rendered under body DIVs rather than document.head on both sampled service pages. The optional auth playbook also found wildcard non-credentialed CORS instead of explicit credentialed origins.

minor.issue: Auth playbook requirement fails: preflight from the configured frontend/production origin returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * and no Access-Control-Allow-Credentials header, because CORS_ORIGINS='*'. Same-origin preview auth works, but explicit credentialed cross-origin auth is not enabled.

integration_issues.issue: On /product-development and /ai-automation, document.head contains 0 JSON-LD scripts instead of the required 3. The correct Service, BreadcrumbList, and FAQPage payloads exist in the document and use verticalinfinity.in, but all three script elements remain inside body DIVs.

action_items: Insert and clean up the three JSON-LD script nodes in document.head (or use a head-management solution); do not rely on React 19 metadata hoisting for script elements. Recheck both sampled service routes and SPA transitions.
If cross-origin cookie auth is required, replace CORS_ORIGINS='*' with an explicit allowlist including https://verticalinfinity.in and the deployed frontend origin, with credentials enabled.
Re-run the frontend SEO and CORS checks after fixes.
critical_code_review_comments: ServicePage.jsx correctly changes ORIGIN for canonical, og:url, Service URL, organization URL, and breadcrumbs, but React 19's native metadata hoisting covers title/meta/link rather than arbitrary application/ld+json scripts; the current map at lines 74-76 therefore leaves scripts in the body.

server.py intentionally disables allow_credentials whenever '*' is configured. This avoids an invalid wildcard-plus-credentials response, but does not satisfy the auth playbook's explicit-origin credentialed CORS requirement.

success_rate.frontend: 83% of requested regression areas; JSON-LD head placement failed on 2/2 sampled service pages

seed_data_creation: Created transient TEST_ contact leads, HTML/script payload leads, a seed-update admin probe, a unique lockout identity, and one UI form lead. All were deleted; verified 0 matching test contacts, users, and login-attempt records remain.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Passing backend coverage: valid/minimal contact creation with status new and persistence; raw HTML/script payload creation and authenticated retrieval; lead_alert_html escaping assertions; whitespace and invalid-email 422 validation; unauthenticated lead-list 401; admin login with secure httpOnly access/refresh token cookies; authenticated lead retrieval; bcrypt $2b$ hash; indexes; five-failure lockout; seed_admin stale-password update. Passing frontend coverage: canonical and og:url use verticalinfinity.in on both sample pages; all three JSON-LD payload contents use the production domain; card 02 click plus real Tab-to-card/Enter navigation; cards 01/03 routing; product contact success toast/Sent state/field reset; production build. Only JSON-LD head placement and optional credentialed CORS remain.
rca_of_the_issue: JSON-LD RCA: React leaves the application/ld+json script elements where ServicePage renders them in the component tree; only title/meta/link receive native metadata hoisting, so document.head has zero scripts while body has all three. CORS RCA: backend/.env configures CORS_ORIGINS='*', and server.py sets allow_credentials to false for wildcard origins, yielding '*' without credential support.
